Choose a resource for the task in front of you. You do not need to set up every template before starting the doctorate.

Use a checklist before starting a study, analysing data or submitting your work. Each one helps you catch omissions while there's still time to fix them.

## Find a useful starting point

| What you need to do | Open this | Leave with |
|---|---|---|
| Prepare for a supervision meeting | [Meeting agenda](templates/meeting-agenda.qmd) | The decisions and questions you want to discuss |
| Turn reading into an argument | [Synthesis and argument map](templates/synthesis-argument-map.qmd) | A provisional answer linked to evidence and limits |
| Ask for focused feedback | [Review cover note](templates/supervisor-review-cover-note.qmd) | A clear request for the next kind of review |
| Choose between methods | [Method-options table](templates/method-options.qmd) | A comparison you can take to an adviser |
| Follow up work that is waiting | [Action register](templates/action-register.qmd) | A named decision owner and follow-up date |
| Work out where to begin | [I'm stuck](stuck/index.qmd) | One next action or a route to help |

Copy only the fields that serve the decision, keeping required approvals and records intact. Worked examples show one way to complete a resource; they are not evidence about your own project. Keep private research material in its approved location, away from public suggestions or shared examples.
